# Demultiplexer

`maiman.components.Demultiplexer` · category **Passive** · [all components](index.md)

One fibre in, one channel out of each port. The receive end of a WDM link.

Every output carries the same filter as `maiman.components.OpticalFilter`
— literally the same function — tuned to its own channel. So a neighbour's
leakage into a port is the super-Gaussian's skirt at the declared spacing,
floored by `extinction`, and it is a number this produces rather than an
assumption it makes: narrow the spacing and the crosstalk rises on its own.

A band that falls between two channels is attenuated by both and appears on
both, which is the right answer and is what a misconfigured plan looks like
from the receive end.

## Ports

| Port | Direction | Type |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `in` | input | optical |
| `out0` | output | optical |
| `out1` | output | optical |
| `out2` | output | optical |
| `out3` | output | optical |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `first_wavelength` | `1550.0` | nm | 1200.0 … 1700.0 | Channel 0. The rest are stepped from it up in frequency, down in wavelength |
| `spacing` | `100.0` | GHz | 1.0 …  | Channel spacing, in frequency because the grid is |
| `wavelength_spacing` | `0.0` | nm | 0.0 …  | A coarse grid's step in wavelength (CWDM: 20 nm), replacing `spacing`; 0 is off |
| `bandwidth` | `50.0` | GHz | 0.0 …  | 3 dB full width of each channel's passband |
| `order` | `3.0` |  | 1.0 … 10.0 | Super-Gaussian order; 3 to 5 is an AWG |
| `insertion_loss` | `4.0` | dB | 0.0 …  | Loss per channel. An AWG routes, so this does not grow with the count |
| `extinction` | `40.0` | dB | 0.0 …  | Out-of-band rejection floor; 0 disables the floor |

## Constructor arguments

Set when the block is created, not swept: `channels`.
